items.title: doc(id): state the #4592 replication admission contract in replication.rs (#4593)
items.body:
Phase 3 (closing audit) of design #4592, for issue #4593 (task 14247).

## What

- States the #4592 admission contract verbatim in the pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs module doc (new 'Admission contract (#4592)' section): a frame is admitted only if its header version names a chain that could exist — inside the restore range JOURNAL_VERSION..=MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION, and, for a snapshot, never lower than the version of the chain the tracker already holds.
- Cross-references the contract from the ReplicationTracker::accept doc comment.
- Documentation only; no behavior change.

## Audit outcome (full inventory posted on issue #4593)

Every WorldCore::restore precondition was dispositioned against accept at origin/main 1cd22df899. Header presence/shape, header world, header version range, per-entry decodability, and payload header agreement (#4486) all hold at accept. Dispositions (b), (c), (d) confirmed with code/test evidence on issue #4593. One confirmed gap: per-entry version requirements (disposition (a)) are enforced at restore (core.rs) but not at accept — filed as follow-up issue #7970, not fixed here per the audit scope.

## Tests

- cargo test -p id --lib world::replication on the laptop (result recorded on issue #4593 / task 14247).

Updates `wrangler` from 4.147.0 to 4.166.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.166.0

Minor Changes

  • #16961 bf7568a Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Show configured trigger targets during experimental wrangler triggers deploy --dry-run

    Dry runs now print a "Would deploy" summary of routes, custom domains, cron schedules, Queue producers and consumers, Workflows, event triggers, and Email Routing addresses instead of exiting without a summary. Explicitly empty cron schedules and Email Routing addresses are shown as removals. The preview makes no API requests or authentication checks; when workers.dev is enabled, it reports that setting without looking up the account's subdomain.

  • #16679 be6aa81 Thanks @​mglewis! - Add images.url_transformations to the Wrangler configuration

    The images block now accepts a url_transformations object for controlling /cdn-cgi/image/ transformations on requests served by a Worker. enabled is required, and allowed_origins optionally lists the origins images may be fetched from (use ["*"] to allow any origin). binding is now optional, so url_transformations can be configured without an Images binding:

    {
  "images": {
    "url_transformations": {
      "enabled": true,
      "allowed_origins": ["images.example.com"]
    }
  }
}

    Like the rest of the images block, url_transformations is not inherited by named environments, and must be specified in each environment that needs it.

    cloudflare.config.ts gains the equivalent setting as a top-level images field on the Worker, with the Images binding remaining in env:

    export default defineConfig({
  worker: {
    name: "my-worker",
    compatibilityDate: "2026-11-01",
    images: {
      urlTransformations: {
        enabled: true,
        allowedOrigins: ["images.example.com"],
      },
    },
  },
});

    cf migrate carries images.url_transformations over to this field.

    This change adds configuration and validation only. url_transformations is not supported in previews.

  • #14114 dce615c Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Add --show-diff flag to wrangler triggers deploy

    When --show-diff is passed, the command fetches the currently deployed trigger configuration from the remote worker and displays a colored diff against the local configuration before deploying. This covers routes, custom domains, cron schedules, and the workers_dev/preview_urls subdomain settings. Route and custom-domain lists are fetched only when that category has local entries to deploy, avoiding unnecessary permission requirements. Queue consumers and event triggers are not compared.

    The flag also works with --dry-run to preview these changes without actually deploying. Displaying a diff requires authentication, including during a dry run.

items.title: docs(mcpx): document published install channels and service modes
items.body: The Install chapter described the first tag and container publication as future work. The release published three archives plus SHA256SUMS on October 30. The November 17 dispatch published the image, and the package API now returns both 0.1.0 and latest at sha256:81566c90a88149be8b995bfa8d3fc515f01e56eb418a7fdfe3213c91e7e5ff9c. This revision documents the actual per-user installer, per-host flag, checksums, the version-specific Docker command, and the managed systemd/launchd options. The archive, original publication run and package are linked beside the channels in the chapter. Fleet verification targets a throwaway prefix and compares the version from the release binary and the independently pulled image. Refs #1881, #9900, #13264. ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-23T18:18:52Z", "session_id": null, "lane": null, "host": "amd", "worktree": "/home/user/wt-mcpx-install-1881", "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": { "kind": "worktree", "id": "/home/user/wt-mcpx-install-1881", "repo": "developing-today/code", "branch": "docs/mcpx-install-receipts-1881", "sha": "73570937179b20caedec4985bfcfe0cc7d400148" }, "auth_subject": "agent-next-19-local", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(mcpx): run examples tests in nix build check phase (#4115)
items.body: ## Summary ```diff checkExclude = [ "internal/e2e" "internal/settings" "internal/cli" "internal/conformance" "internal/defaults" - "examples" # interim #2896 exclusion; its fix landed in #2943 ]; ``` Removes only the expired `examples` exclusion. The other `checkExclude` entries remain untouched. ## Evidence - **Before:** `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix` excluded `examples` under an interim comment directing removal after #2896. - **After:** the exclusion and comment are removed; `git diff --check` passes. Local `nix build .#mcpx --print-build-logs` is running and will verify that examples are included in the check phase. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way **Blast Radius:** narrow This adds the examples package back to the Nix build check phase; a failing test will fail the build instead of being silently skipped. Fixes #4115. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

Updates `wrangler` from 4.147.0 to 4.152.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.151.3

Patch Changes

  • #15611 4508172 Thanks @​taylorlee! - Allow wrangler dev to start module Workers without a default export

    Previously, wrangler dev failed to start module Workers that exported only named entrypoints, such as RPC services, unless an unused default export was added. These Workers now start normally in local development without that workaround.

  • #16370 61fc739 Thanks @​WalshyDev! - Fetch the remote config diff from the configured compliance region

    When a Worker was last deployed from the dashboard, wrangler deploy and wrangler versions upload download its remote configuration to compare with the local one. These requests ignored the compliance_region field in the Wrangler configuration file and only honoured the CLOUDFLARE_COMPLIANCE_REGION environment variable. A FedRAMP High Worker configured through the config file would send them to api.cloudflare.com instead of api.fed.cloudflare.com, and the deploy would fail with authentication errors. They now use the same compliance region as the rest of the deploy.

  • #15846 a88cac4 Thanks @​oddharsh! - Fail with an error instead of hanging when local dev requests can't work under Bun

    Bun's fetch() ignores the undici dispatcheroven-sh/bun#39247createTestHarness()'s server.fetch() and server.getWorker()'s fetch(), email() and scheduled() now throw a UserError, requests to the dev server URL get a 503 naming the cause, and starting remote bindings throws a UserError. Each of these used to hang with no error. server.getWorker().getEnv() and getExport() keep working under Bun.

  • #16359 262021d Thanks @​tw4! - Stop --strict deploys and version uploads from aborting when the API omits optional binding fields

    Previously, wrangler deploy --strict and wrangler versions upload --strict could report a destructive change for an unchanged configuration, for example an R2 bucket in the default jurisdiction, because a field the API left out was compared as removed. Missing and unset optional fields are now treated as equal, so these commands proceed when the local configuration matches the deployed Worker.
